A1.justification: Both PDFs describe VidTwin. Their text, equations, tables, figures, and complete appendices support reliable comparison, including matching material relocated between versions.

before.justification: v1 reports original reconstruction experiments, human evaluations, component ablations, scaling experiments, resource measurements, and UCF-101 generation results.

after.justification: v2 retains these original results and adds reconstruction comparisons, compression-rate experiments, temporal robustness evaluations, and a failure case.

M1.justification: The Q-Former structure branch, convolution-and-averaging dynamics branch, additive decoding, VAE losses, and diffusion-model adaptation remain unchanged. The additional compression configurations evaluate the existing architecture rather than introduce a new method component.

E1.justification: The self-collected training data, MCL-JCV reconstruction task, and UCF-101 generation task are retained. Appendix B.3 adds temporal test scenarios involving longer, 32-frame clips and higher-frame-rate, 40-FPS video.

E2.justification: v2 adds CV-VAE to the main reconstruction comparison in Table 1. New Table 5 evaluates CV-VAE, OD-VAE, Open-Sora, and CogVideoX against VidTwin, substantially broadening the reconstruction comparator set. The generation comparators in Table 2 remain unchanged.

E3.justification: The original 16-frame, 224-resolution, 25-FPS reconstruction evaluation is retained. Added experiments evaluate four compression ratios and introduce 32-frame and 40-FPS user-study conditions using the existing subjective-evaluation subset. These are additional settings, not evidence that the original experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: v2 adds a compression-versus-reconstruction sensitivity study in Table 6, temporal robustness evaluations in Table 7, and a basketball failure case in Figure 6. These substantially broaden analysis of design trade-offs and failure conditions. The original component ablations, scaling experiment, and latent-intervention examples are retained.

E5.justification: Both versions report point estimates and mean opinion scores without adding repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, or significance tests. The new subjective-evaluation rows retain the existing point-score reporting practice.

E6.justification: The original scores in Tables 1–4 are retained, including VidTwin's 28.137 reconstruction PSNR and generation FVD of 193. v2 adds comparator scores, compression-quality results ranging from PSNR 24.41 at 0.11% to 30.04 at 0.48%, and temporal-evaluation scores. These substantially expand the results; the compression variants do not establish a same-setting performance improvement.

T1.justification: The method equations and VAE/diffusion derivations are retained, with the background appendix moving from D to E. Appendix B.1 restates the compression-ratio definition already present in v1 Section 4.2; it does not introduce a new mathematical definition or theoretical result.

C1.justification: The substantive claims about decoupled latents, compression, reconstruction, downstream generation, explainability, and scalability remain unchanged. Removing 'foundation' from the introduction and conclusion does not change the stated capabilities or technical contributions.

C2.justification: Appendix A.2 newly clarifies that complete disentanglement is not the objective and cross-reenactment is illustrative. Appendix B.4 explains failure under extremely rapid motion and proposes future training adaptations. Appendix B.1 also adds a trade-off interpretation, but incorrectly says lower latent/input ratios improve reconstruction, contradicting Table 6.

D1.justification: v2 explicitly identifies the default latent configuration for otherwise unspecified results, adds CV-VAE implementation information, and updates project/demo access pointers. Existing optimizer, hardware, training, and latent-size details are retained after relocation. The PDFs do not establish a change in underlying resource availability.

R1.justification: v2 adds citations to CV-VAE, OD-VAE, WF-VAE, CogVideoX, Open-Sora, and Open-Sora Plan, and briefly positions concurrent approaches as predominantly using uniform-size frame latents. The existing related-work narrative remains largely intact. The updated Video In-Context Learning reference represents the same work.

P1.justification: The main narrative receives limited editing and an acknowledgments section. The appendices gain a separate analysis section, with scalability moving from A.4 to B.2 and former Appendices B–D becoming C–E. These are localized expansions and reorganization rather than extensive rewriting.

P2.justification: Table 1 gains a CV-VAE row, and v2 adds Tables 5–7 and the failure-case Figure 6. Existing reconstruction and cross-reenactment figures are relocated and renumbered. Other visual refinements include temporal labels, resizing, and correcting Figure 2's 'Average on weight' to 'Average on width'; the overall layout remains similar.

improvement.justification: The newer baselines and compression/temporal tests strengthen empirical support, while explicit discussion of incomplete disentanglement and fast-motion failure clarifies limitations. However, the added experiments are only briefly specified, and Appendix B.1 reverses the compression-quality trend shown in Table 6. The additions provide a useful but limited net improvement.
